context: You will hear a radio presenter talking about a local festival.

script.t: Good evening, and welcome to What's On. This week I'm looking at the Harbourside Festival, which returns next week for its twentieth year.
The festival runs for six days, from Tuesday to Sunday, and most events are free, although you'll need tickets for the evening concerts.
Let me go through some of the highlights. On Tuesday, the festival opens with a parade through the old town, starting at six. This year's theme is the sea, so expect plenty of costumes and boats.
Wednesday is family day, with a puppet theatre in the main square. Originally there was going to be a magic show as well, but unfortunately the performer has had to cancel.
If you're interested in food, Thursday is the day for you. Around forty local producers will be running a market along the waterfront, and there'll be cooking demonstrations every hour.
On Friday evening, there's an outdoor film screening on the beach. Bring a blanket, because it can get cold once the sun goes down.
The big concert is on Saturday night, featuring the city's youth orchestra. Tickets are fifteen dollars, or ten for students, and they're selling fast.
And on Sunday, the festival ends with fireworks over the harbour at nine thirty.
A few practical tips. Parking near the harbour will be very limited, so the organisers strongly recommend using the free shuttle bus from the central station, which runs every twenty minutes.
If you'd like to help, the festival still needs volunteers, especially for the Saturday concert. Volunteers get a free festival T-shirt and a meal voucher.
The full programme is available on the festival website, and printed copies can be picked up from the tourist information office.
